title: Shared $defs for the afb.execution.v1 wire protocol and AFB-internal schemas
description: Building blocks reused across deal.v2.json/tradeplan.v2.json/condition.v1.json/instrument.v1.json and payloads/dataset.*.json. Extracted from the former deal.v1.json (2026-08-11); deal.v1/tradeplan.v1 have since been removed.

dealStatus.description: Deal status — the single vocabulary of deal_state.v2.json `status` (kept equal by a test) used by the afbws deal/tradeplan channels. Deletion is not a status.

executionPhase.description: Execution phase of a deal — the single vocabulary of deal_state.v2.json `execution_phase` (kept equal by a test).

legId.description: Stable identity of a tradeplan leg across edits — the key overrides/carry-over (tradeplan/deal separation Фаза B2) use to match a plan leg to its compiled deal leg, never array position. Assigned once when a leg is created and never reused/reassigned. Shared by tradeplan.v2.json (stored/channel legs) and afbws/deal.public.v1.json (the plan-leg identity projected onto deal legs). Legacy synthetic ids (`legacy:{role}:{index}`) are NOT part of the contract: a plan leg without `leg_id` exists only in an input message (the server assigns one on save) or in an old stored file (the server back-fills it on the next write).

tradeplanId.description: Id of an AFB tradeplan (state/tradeplans/<user_id>/<id>.yaml). Opaque, case-sensitive. Shared by tradeplan.v2.json, afbws/tradeplan.channel.v2.json and gp.v2.json (`tradeplan_id`, the owning plan of a primitive).

source.description: Provenance of this deal's compiled definition. The AFB compiler writes only `tradeplan_id` — the single source of truth for deal->tradeplan linkage (see the tradeplan/deal separation plan). `kind`/`draft_id` are a deprecated pre-separation pair: new AFB never writes them, they may still appear on persisted records created before the deal-channel-migration offline backfill ran. Left open (no additionalProperties restriction, matching the rest of this wire schema) since AFB may carry extra compile metadata here (e.g. `compiled_at`, `primitive_snapshot`, and — Фаза B2 — `leg_ids` [{entry,stop_loss,take_profit}: [leg_id|null, ...], parallel to the matching deal.v2.json leg array] and `removed_plan_leg_ids` [string[], tombstoned plan leg_ids]) that BF does not interpret; AFB's own public projection reduces this object to `tradeplan_id` alone (afbws/deal.public.v1.json#/$defs/source) — the only piece that survives elsewhere is `leg_ids`, re-projected per leg as `leg_id` on the public v2 legs (afbws/deal.public.v1.json#/$defs/legId), never as part of `source`.

tradeplan_id.description: Id of the AFB tradeplan (state/tradeplans/<user_id>/<id>.yaml) that compiled this deal.

kind.description: Deprecated legacy discriminator (always 'tradeplan_draft'). New AFB never writes this.

draft_id.description: Deprecated alias of tradeplan_id predating the tradeplan/deal separation. New AFB never writes this.

instrumentAddress.description: Venue address of an instrument WITHOUT the catalog key: the `exchange/board/ticker` triple as a party that has no instrument catalog can state it. Used only where the object is formed by BF (BF has no catalog and does not know `instrument_key`) — today payloads/dataset.subscribe.json (bf2afb, reserved). The triple is an address, not an identity; AFB translates it into an `instrument_key` once, at the boundary. Objects formed by AFB use `#/$defs/instrument`, where the key is mandatory.

exchange.description: Venue MIC as in the AFB catalog (e.g. `MISX`).

board.description: Venue board; may be an empty string where the venue has none.

instrument.description: Instrument of an object formed by AFB (deal `target.instrument`, a dataset.update record). IDENTITY is `instrument_key` alone (mandatory). The `exchange/board/ticker` triple is the VENUE ADDRESS, not an identity: BF cross-checks it against the instrument the broker returned for `broker_symbol` (`instrument_mismatch`) and it is part of `definition_hash`; `instrument_key` is NOT part of `definition_hash` and BF does not interpret it (BF code is unaware of the field and carries it through untouched).

exchange.description: Venue address: MIC as in the AFB catalog (e.g. `MISX`).

board.description: Venue address: board; may be an empty string where the venue has none.

ticker.description: Venue address: ticker. Case-sensitive, never normalized. Not an identifier.

instrument_key.description: Full catalog key of the instrument (`<MIC>[:<board|market>]:<ticker>`) — its only identity, mandatory. Case-sensitive, never normalized. Decides whether the instrument changed on an amend (amend_rules falls back to the venue triple only when a deal stored by BF before the key became mandatory lacks it).

broker_symbol.description: Opaque broker locator of the instrument, e.g. `TICKER@MIC`. AFB takes it from its catalog (the instrument's address at the account's broker); BF resolves the instrument ONLY by it (no BF-side catalog). Not part of the instrument identity (that is `instrument_key`), see amend_rules. Absent => BF rejects with instrument_unresolvable unless the deal binding already carries a symbol.

binding.description: broker-native locator added by BF after publish

account_id.description: Broker account this deal is published against. Optional on the wire — absent means BF's own trading account (brokers/port.py::account_id). AFB compiles it from the owning tradeplan's publish.account_id (see tradeplan.v2.json publish), resolving empty/absent to the connector's default account before publish (ExecutionService.resolve_plan_account). BF validates it against its own account (plan_engine/plan_validation.py: wrong_account_id) when present.

execution_mode.description: How exit protection is executed. Absent means `client` (condition engine only, current behaviour). `hybrid` additionally places a server-side SLTP backstop order once a position opens. `server` is reserved — not yet implemented by any BF, always rejected at publish. See RESILIENCE.md, Фаза 3/5.

backstop.description: Per-deal overrides for the hybrid-mode server-side backstop order; unset fields fall back to the executing BF's own config defaults. Meaningful only when execution_mode is `hybrid`.

take_profit.description: Reserved for a future server-side take-profit leg (OCO). Always rejected as true for now — the backstop is protection-only in this phase.
